summary: The area's only roadmap, tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/HopfRinow (5 layers), states its hypotheses correctly: finite dimension, no boundary, C^∞ data, and connectedness where it is needed. The red team found no false layer statement. It found 16 findings, one of them high. The Hopf–Rinow step (a_p) ⇒ (f_p) cannot be completed from what Layers 1–2 plan: it needs uniformly normal neighbourhoods and 'a minimizing curve is an unbroken geodesic', which no layer plans. The proof path also lacks the fundamental theorem on flows (open maximal flow domain, smooth flow), which LieGroups and HeegaardFloer need as well; the symmetry lemma for two-parameter maps; and uniqueness of geodesics on closed intervals. The roadmap text is stale against the pinned libraries. Mathlib 082e2d3 has Levi-Civita existence and uniqueness and `IsMetricCompatible`, so the planned shim is obsolete. Tau Ceti f790474 has most of Layer 0, the connection, spray and ODE half of Layer 1, and Layer 4's metric API. The atlas records none of this, and no stage edge to the three roadmaps that consume HopfRinow. The do Carmo locators are cited from the print edition; no public copy exists.

findings.claim: The (a_p) => (f_p) step cannot be completed from what Layers 1-2 plan. In the do Carmo argument the roadmap follows (minimize d(.,q) on a normal sphere, then extend along gamma(s) = exp_p(s v)), the inductive step at s0 produces a broken curve p -> gamma(s0) -> x0' of length s0 + delta' = d(p, x0') and must conclude x0' = gamma(s0 + delta'), i.e. that a length-minimizing piecewise-C1 curve has no corner. Layer 2 plans, for each point separately, a normal ball of some radius, with no lower bound on the radii at nearby points, and its minimization and equality statements apply only to curves starting at that ball's centre; the corner gamma(s0) is an interior point of the curve, so removing it needs a normal ball of radius > epsilon + delta' centred at a nearby point (gamma(s0 - epsilon) or x0'), i.e. a lower bound on normal radii near gamma(s0). That is the totally (uniformly) normal neighbourhood theorem, built from the inverse function theorem for (q, v) -> (q, exp_q v) on TM at (p, 0), and its consequence that a minimizing piecewise-C1 curve parametrized proportionally to arc length is an unbroken geodesic. No layer plans either, and the one alternative route (first variation for piecewise curves) is explicitly declared not an input and is restricted to smooth curves.
findings.evidence: Roadmap, tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/HopfRinow#layer-3-the-hopfrinow-equivalence: 'Build it by minimizing distance on compact spheres in the finite-dimensional `T_p M`, using continuity of distance to `q`, and iterating the normal-ball radial extension step.' tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/HopfRinow#layer-2-normal-neighbourhoods-the-gauss-lemma-and-minimizing-geodesics: normal neighbourhoods only at the fixed point: '`exp_p` restricts to a diffeomorphism from a star-shaped neighbourhood of `0`, giving normal balls and normal coordinates'; first variation: 'define the energy functional on `C¹` curves', 'prove that a smooth curve is critical exactly when it is a geodesic', and 'This milestone is part of the reusable geodesic API; it is not an input to the Hopf–Rinow implication graph below.' The README References cite do Carmo '**§4** (convex neighbourhoods)' but no layer plans them. Sources: do Carmo, Riemannian Geometry (1992, print; no public copy), Ch. 3 Theorem 3.7 (totally normal neighbourhood W with exp_q a diffeomorphism on B_delta(0) and exp_q(B_delta(0)) containing W for every q in W) and Corollary 3.9 (a piecewise differentiable curve with parameter proportional to arc length and length <= that of every competitor is a geodesic), the latter invoked in the proof of Ch. 7 Theorem 2.8 for exactly this step. Lee, Introduction to Riemannian Manifolds, 2nd ed., public front matter (read 2026-09-24): contents 'Uniformly Normal Neighborhoods ... 163' placed before 'Completeness ... 166' in Ch. 6, and preface: 'some elementary ideas from the calculus of variations are introduced to prove that every distance-minimizing curve is a geodesic'; public errata, entry 'Page 165, proof of Theorem 6.15': 'the definition of uniformly normal neighborhood implies that the image of γ|[a,b] is contained in a geodesic ball centered at γ(a)'. Libraries: Tau Ceti f790474, no exponential map, normal or uniformly normal neighbourhood (git grep -i 'expDomain|expMap|totally normal|uniformly normal|normal ball' over TauCeti returns nothing); Mathlib 082e2d3, no Riemannian geodesics in Mathlib/Geometry.

findings.claim: Layer 1 plans only a local geodesic flow, but its exponential-map milestones use 'the open subset of the geodesic-flow domain', i.e. they presuppose the fundamental theorem on flows: the maximal flow domain {(t, z) : t in J(z)} is open in R x TM and the maximal flow is C^infinity on it. That theorem, not a local flow near t = 0, is what gives IsOpen (expDomain p) and smoothness of exp_p at vectors far from 0 (used in (a_p) and (f_p) => (b) on closedBall 0 r for large r, and in the Gauss lemma on a whole normal ball), and it also gives the joint exponential map exp on the open set {v in TM : 1 in J(v)}, which the uniform-normal-neighbourhood step and OptimalTransport Layer 7 (x -> exp_x(-t • ∇φ x)) need but Layer 1 plans only fibrewise. Neither library has it: Tau Ceti's smooth dependence is a model-space result that is C^(n+1) only at the single point (a, 0), and its maximal integral curves carry no dependence on the initial point. The general-vector-field theorem is also needed by LieGroups Layer 4 (Frobenius) and HeegaardFloer Lane M (gradient flows); the accepted LieGroups link map assigns it to 'HopfRinow, Part II', a roadmap that does not exist.

findings.claim: The Gauss lemma needs covariant differentiation along a two-parameter map f(t,s) (for f(t,s) = exp_p(t (v + s w))) and the symmetry lemma D_s ∂_t f = D_t ∂_s f, which follows from torsion-freeness. Layer 2 names neither as a prerequisite of the Gauss lemma. The only mention of two-parameter differentiation is inside the first-variation milestone, which the roadmap declares 'not an input to the Hopf–Rinow implication graph', and the symmetry lemma is not named anywhere. As written, the dependency is backwards: the machinery the Gauss lemma needs sits in a milestone marked as not feeding Hopf–Rinow.
findings.evidence: Roadmap, tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/HopfRinow#layer-2-normal-neighbourhoods-the-gauss-lemma-and-minimizing-geodesics: 'The Gauss lemma: prove the radial/tangential orthogonality identity for `mfderiv exp_p` and its polar length inequality on a normal ball' (no prerequisite named); first variation: 'Build covariant differentiation in both variation directions, prove the integration-by-parts step and the first-variation formula' and 'This milestone is part of the reusable geodesic API; it is not an input to the Hopf–Rinow implication graph below.' Source: do Carmo, Riemannian Geometry (1992, print), Ch. 3 §3: the symmetry lemma for a parametrized surface (Lemma 3.4) is used in the proof of the Gauss lemma (Lemma 3.5). Lee IRM 2nd ed. public front matter (2026-09-24): Ch. 6 'Geodesics and Minimizing Curves' (p. 151) develops the variational machinery first, and the preface says 'Then the Gauss lemma is used to prove the (partial) converse'. findings.claim: Uniqueness of geodesics, and everything built on it (J(p,v) as a single curve, exp_p, the extension step of (c) => (d)), goes through uniqueness of integral curves of the spray on TM. That needs TM to be Hausdorff. The roadmap's standing hypotheses give only [T2Space M], and neither pinned library derives T2Space (TangentBundle I M), or Hausdorffness of any fibre-bundle total space, from T2Space of the base. Tau Ceti's geodesic uniqueness therefore carries an extra hypothesis [T2Space (TangentBundle I M)] that the roadmap's hypotheses do not supply.

findings.claim: Layer 1 plans uniqueness of geodesics only on open intervals, but Layers 2-3 work with geodesics on closed intervals whose initial data sit at an endpoint. (f_p) is stated with IsGeodesicCurveOn γ (Icc 0 1), γ 0 = p, and '(a_p) and (f_p) => (b)' needs every such witness to satisfy γ 1 = exp_p v, where v is its one-sided initial velocity, to obtain closedBall p r = exp_p '' closedBall 0 r. This needs uniqueness (or extendability) of a geodesic on Icc 0 b with data at the endpoint 0: such a geodesic is the restriction of the maximal geodesic with data (p, v), and [0, b] ⊆ J(p, v). Neither library has this. Mathlib's manifold uniqueness is on Ioo or global, and Tau Ceti's geodesic uniqueness is on Ioo only.

findings.claim: The roadmap asserts that the pinned Mathlib lacks CovariantDerivative.IsMetricCompatible, and it instructs defining a local shim and proving existence and uniqueness of the Levi-Civita connection. At the pinned baseline (Mathlib 082e2d3, the revision Tau Ceti f790474 pins), Metric.lean and LeviCivita.lean are present. Mathlib defines IsMetricCompatible and IsLeviCivitaConnection, constructs leviCivitaConnection, proves it metric-compatible and torsion-free, and proves uniqueness on differentiable vector fields. The shim instruction would now create a duplicate, and the existence-and-uniqueness milestone is built. Only regularity was left to future work, and Tau Ceti built it.

findings.claim: Most Layer 1 targets are built at the pinned Tau Ceti. The roadmap text still says some are absent: the finite-endpoint extension criterion ('the pinned integral-curve API has no maximal-solution extension theorem'), the manifold inverse function theorem ('this roadmap owns it as a prerequisite') and C^k dependence ('not a theorem available in the pinned ODE library'). Built: the along-curve derivative with linearity, Leibniz, locality, reparametrization, pullback agreement and the chart formula; IsGeodesicCurveOn with initial data and its chart ODE; the geodesic spray with its chart-change law, C^infinity regularity and integral curves equal to velocity lifts; local existence and open-interval uniqueness; constant speed; J(p,v), which is open and order-connected, contains 0 and satisfies t ∈ J(p, a•v) ↔ a t ∈ J(p,v) for a ≠ 0; maximal integral curves with the extension criterion at both endpoints; the manifold inverse function theorem; and a model-space C^(n+1) local flow. Still missing: the chosen maximal geodesic and the homogeneity identity itself, the smooth flow on TM, expDomain and exp_p with their derivative at 0, and (a_p) ↔ (d_p).

findings.claim: The roadmap calls [ConnectedSpace M] load-bearing wherever used, and Layer 3 assumes it together with an existing [MetricSpace M] and [IsRiemannianManifold I M]. The (b) => (e_p) step also invokes 'connectedness and finiteness of dist', but ⋃ n, closedBall p n = univ holds in any metric space.

findings.claim: HopfRinow Layer 4 defines smooth Riemannian isometries for 'downstream roadmaps (constant-curvature model spaces)'. GeometricTopology Layers 7-8 use Riemannian isometries (volume invariance, the maximal isometry groups of the eight model geometries) without naming a supplier, so no link stops them from defining a second notion. GeometricTopology Layer 8 also needs Isom(X) to be a Lie group, which for metric isometries requires the Myers–Steenrod theorem. HopfRinow says Myers–Steenrod 'would be a separate owned milestone', and no layer in the atlas owns it.
findings.evidence: Roadmap, tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/HopfRinow#layer-4-corollaries-and-downstream-theory: 'Transport across smooth Riemannian isometries: define a smooth Riemannian isometry ...', 'including transport through the `IsRiemannianManifold` identification for downstream roadmaps (constant-curvature model spaces)', 'obtaining the required smoothness from metric preservation is a Myers–Steenrod theorem, which would be a separate owned milestone'. GeometricTopology Layer 7: 'The **Riemannian volume measure** ... and its invariance under isometries'; Layer 8: 'The **eight model geometries** as homogeneous Riemannian 3-manifolds `(X, Isom X)` ... each with its maximal isometry group' and '-- structure ModelGeometry where X : Manifold …; isom : LieGroup …'. At f790474 and 082e2d3 no Riemannian isometry notion exists (git grep -i isometr over TauCeti/Geometry/Manifold and Mathlib/Geometry/Manifold finds only linear isometries).
